title: Overhead Crane Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.179)
subtitle: For frequent and periodic crane inspections, monthly hook, chain and rope checks, and cranes returning from idle.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is marked Defect, decide whether it is a safety hazard and keep the crane out of operation until designated personnel correct any unsafe condition (1910.179(l)(3)(i)).
The crane manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Frequent inspection items
items: All functional operating mechanisms work with no maladjustment interfering with proper operation
No deterioration or leakage in lines, tanks, valves, drain pumps or other air or hydraulic parts
No cracks or deformation; throat opening no more than 15 percent over normal; twist no more than 10° from the plane of the unbent hook
Certification record for the latest monthly inspection with date, inspector's signature and hook serial number or other identifier
No excessive wear, twist or distorted links interfering with function; stretch within manufacturer limits
Monthly record with date, signature and chain identifier
No excessive wear of components in functional operating mechanisms
Reeving matches the crane manufacturer's recommendations

sections.title: Periodic inspection items (check section A too)
items: No deformed, cracked or corroded members
No cracked or worn sheaves or drums
No worn, cracked or distorted pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers, locking or clamping devices
No excessive wear on brake parts, linings, pawls or ratchets
No significant inaccuracy over the full range
Gasoline, diesel, electric or other powerplant performs properly and meets applicable safety requirements
No excessive sprocket wear or chain stretch
No pitting or deterioration of controller contactors, limit switches or pushbutton stations

sections.title: Running ropes and drum
items: Not reduced below nominal by loss of core support, corrosion or wear of outside wires
Number and concentration of broken outside wires checked and judged not to be a hazard
No worn outside wires causing appreciable loss of strength
No corroded or broken wires at end connections
No corroded, cracked, bent, worn or improperly applied end connections
No severe kinking, crushing, cutting or unstranding
At least two wraps remain on the drum with the hook at its extreme low position
Record on file showing date, signature and the ropes inspected

sections.title: Markings, controls and safety devices
items: Rated load plainly marked on each side of the crane; each hoist's rated load on the hoist or load block, legible from the floor
Box protects against electrical shock; every function clearly marked
Each button returns to off when pressure is released
Tried under no load with the block inched in or run at slow speed; switch operates
Gong or other effective warning signal works (not required on floor-operated cranes)
Switch or circuit breaker on a fixed structure, reachable from the floor, can be locked open
Exposed gears, set screws, projecting keys, chains and sprockets are guarded
Stops in place at the limits of trolley travel
Bridge trucks have sweeps extending below the top of the rail and projecting in front of the wheels

references: 29 CFR 1910.179: Overhead and gantry cranes (Part 1910 Subpart N, Materials Handling and Storage)
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
